guardian.name: Chacha Chowrangi
guardian.personality: A Karachi roundabout who has watched every rickshaw, minibus and donkey cart circle him for sixty years. Unhurried, fond, a little hoarse from the horns; calls everyone beta and treats road safety like family honour.
guardian.voice: Older male or gender-neutral, gravelly and slow, warm Karachi Urdu-English lilt, like a chaiwala chatting at dusk.
descriptions: a photo of a busy Karachi street with rickshaws, minibuses, motorbikes and carts sharing the road
a colourful South Asian vehicle with painted panels, chrome trim, tassels and stickers parked at the roadside
a wooden cart on wheels parked on a market street, loaded with goods, fruit or a cooking setup
a close-up photo of a wheel, tyre, headlight or hand-painted body panel of a vehicle
a vehicle seen from the pavement on a dusty city road with shop signs and overhead wires
a boat, tractor or train seen from a distance against open water, fields or railway tracks

lines.first_meet: [warm chuckle] Salaam, beta. I'm Chacha Chowrangi. Everything with wheels goes round me. Photos from the footpath only, never the road!
lines.again: Back again? [laughs] You're a regular now, like the W-11 at Tower. Chalo, who have you brought me today?
lines.goodbye: Cross at the signal, beta, eyes both ways. [softly] The road is full of stories; just don't stand in the middle of one.
lines.hint: [squints] Hmm, can't tell who that is. From the pavement, show me the whole vehicle, wheels and all. Or its painted back, closer.

characters.name: Pappu Rickshaw
characters.personality: A three-wheeled Karachi hustler who knows every shortcut and gali, talks fast, haggles faster, and is secretly vain about its tassels.
characters.voice: Young-to-middle-aged male, quick and cheeky, slightly nasal, street-smart Karachi patter.
descriptions: a three-wheeled auto rickshaw with a rounded canopy roof and a single front wheel on a city street
a close-up of a rickshaw front with one headlight, a small windscreen, chrome trim and dangling tassels
the back of an auto rickshaw with painted art, slogans and reflective tape under a curved hood
an enclosed rickshaw cabin with a curved roof and side panels, unlike an open flat-roofed cart with facing benches
blue-and-white or green CNG rickshaws parked in a row at a roadside rickshaw stand

lines.first_meet: [revs] Pappu here! My granddad was a smoky Vespa two-stroke; I run on CNG now. Snap me from the footpath, yaar, not the road!
lines.again: [honks] You again? Read my back: 'Pappu yaar tang na kar!' [laughs] Kidding. Wave from the footpath, I'll honk back.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, I've got a gali to squeeze through. [laughs] Go find my cousin the Qingqi. He's the one with nine passengers.

characters.name: Qingqi Bhai
characters.personality: A motorbike that grew a whole drawing room behind it; sociable, cheerful, and has never once said no to one more passenger.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, booming and jolly, a little breathless, bazaar-conductor energy.
descriptions: a motorcycle front joined to an open rear passenger cart with two benches facing each other under a flat roof
a flat canopy roof with colourful hanging fringe over an open cart pulled by a motorbike
a side view showing motorcycle handlebars and fuel tank attached to a long open box with bench seats
an open-sided passenger cart with no doors and no curved hood, unlike an enclosed auto rickshaw
a motorbike front end fixed to a wide two-wheeled rear cart, unlike a plain two-wheeled motorcycle

lines.first_meet: [laughs] Qingqi Bhai! Named after a Chinese bike company, raised in Karachi. Six seats, nine riders. Shoot me from the kerb, okay?
lines.again: Oho, my regular! [cheerful] Squeeze in, there's always room... in the photo, I mean. From the footpath, always.
lines.goodbye: [revs] Chalo, the bazaar won't wait. Go find a thela with a mango pyramid. Tell them Qingqi Bhai sent you.

characters.name: Dulhan Bedford
characters.personality: A Bedford truck dressed like a bride, a poet at heart; recites the couplets painted on her back and thinks of her mother's prayers on long night drives.
characters.voice: Mature and grand, deep and slow with a ghazal-like rhythm; female or gender-neutral, theatrical but tender.
descriptions: a large truck covered in vivid hand-painted flowers, birds, landscapes and calligraphy on every panel
a tall carved wooden crown above a truck cab, decorated with mirrors, painted patterns and small lights
a close-up of a truck's lower edge with dangling metal chains, bells and leaf-shaped pendants
the back of a painted cargo truck with Urdu calligraphy, a portrait panel and mirror mosaic
a painted open wooden cargo body with no passenger windows, unlike a minibus or a plain steel water tank

lines.first_meet: [proudly] They call me dulhan, the bride. Read my back: 'Dekh magar pyar se.' Look, but with love, and from the footpath, jaan.
lines.again: [sighs happily] Back to read me again? Every flower, every couplet, painted freehand by an ustaad. No two of us are alike.
lines.goodbye: [softly] 'Maa ki dua, jannat ki hawa.' My mother's prayer rides with me. Go safely, and call your mother tonight.

characters.name: W-11 Wali
characters.personality: Karachi's loudest minibus, chrome to the roof and proud of every sticker; boastful, musical, shouts its route like a conductor and loves every passenger.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, any gender, loud and rhythmic, a bit hoarse, sing-song conductor calls and a big laugh.
descriptions: a Karachi minibus covered in shiny colourful stickers, chrome panels, mirrors and rows of small lights
a close-up of a decorated bus front with a chrome grille, painted motifs, glittering stickers and a route number
a side view of a minibus with a long row of passenger windows, an open door and a roof rack
a decorated passenger bus with windows and doors along its length, unlike a painted cargo truck with a wooden crown
a stickered minibus at a busy roadside stop under overhead wires and shop signs

lines.first_meet: [shouts] Tower, Tower, Keamari! W-11 here, chrome to the roof. Snap me from the footpath; I don't brake for fans.
lines.again: [laughs] Oho, a regular! I'd give you a free ride, but my conductor would faint. Wave from the kerb, I'll flash my lights.
lines.goodbye: [two loud slaps] Chalo ustaad! That's our signal to move. You move too, onto the footpath. See you at the next stop.

characters.name: Bhola Gadha Gari
characters.personality: A patient donkey cart, quietly the strongest worker in the bazaar; deadpan, dignified, and very tired of donkey jokes.
characters.voice: Older, low and dry, slow deadpan delivery with a gentle sigh.
descriptions: a small flat wooden cart on two car tyres pulled by a donkey on a city street
a donkey harnessed between two wooden shafts in front of a low cart loaded with bricks or water drums
a close-up of a flat plank cart bed on two rubber car tyres with ropes and sacks
a small grey or brown long-eared donkey pulling a cart, much smaller than a camel or a horse
a plain low cart with no hood, plumes or painted panels, pulled by an animal rather than pushed by hand

lines.first_meet: [sighs] Yes, a donkey. Pakistan has millions of us, and we move half the bazaar. Photo from a distance, please, no flash.
lines.again: [snorts] You again. Fine, fine. Don't pat my ears, I'm working. Stand back on the footpath, beta.
lines.goodbye: [slow clip-clop] Off to carry bricks. Go find the camel cart in the old city. He thinks he's taller. He is.

characters.name: Oont Sahib
characters.personality: A towering, unbothered camel cart who considers city traffic beneath its notice; slow, lofty, full of desert wisdom and mild snobbery.
characters.voice: Deep, slow and aristocratic with drawn-out vowels; older male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a large flat wooden platform cart on truck tyres pulled by a tall camel along a road
a camel with a long curved neck and a hump harnessed to a heavily loaded cart
a wide cart piled high with sacks, timber or fodder, much bigger than a donkey cart
a side view of a towering camel above a long low platform cart on rubber tyres

lines.first_meet: [groans slowly] Oont Sahib. I haul what three donkeys can't, and I never hurry. Keep off the road and well back; I kick sideways.
lines.again: [unimpressed] Hmm. You again. Camels remember faces. Yours, I don't mind. Still, stay well back, beta.
lines.goodbye: [yawns] The road is long and I'm in no rush. Go find the sea; I hear the boats there are painted. Show-offs.

characters.name: Victoria Begum
characters.personality: A plumed Victoria carriage from Karachi's grand old days, now waiting for riders by the sea; nostalgic, gracious, a touch dramatic.
characters.voice: Elderly female, refined and nostalgic, slow with theatrical pauses.
descriptions: a decorated two-wheel horse-drawn carriage with a folding black hood and colourful plumes
a close-up of a carriage side with painted panels, brass lamps and a tall spoked wheel
a horse in a decorated harness with feathers and bells standing beside a carriage near a beach
an ornate hooded passenger carriage with lamps and plumes, unlike a plain flat donkey cart

lines.first_meet: [nostalgic sigh] Victoria Begum. Once we filled Saddar's streets; now I wait by the sea. My horse startles, so stay back, dear.
lines.again: [delighted] You remembered me! Hardly anyone does these days. Do get my plumes in, dear. A lady has her best side.
lines.goodbye: [bells jingle] Go on, the sea is right there. Watch the waves, not the road, and give the horses room to walk.

characters.name: Pedal Pehelwan
characters.personality: A heavy black roadster that has hauled milk cans and school bags for decades; humble and steady, puffs uphill, proud of never needing petrol.
characters.voice: Older male, cheerful and slightly creaky, measured pace.
descriptions: a two-wheeled pedal bicycle with a metal frame, chain and handlebars leaning against a wall
a close-up of bicycle pedals, chain and a thin spoked wheel with no engine
a black roadster bicycle with a rear carrier rack and a bell parked beside a railing
a thin-framed bicycle with no fuel tank, exhaust pipe or engine, lighter than a motorcycle

lines.first_meet: [bell rings] Pedal Pehelwan! No petrol, no CNG, just legs. Doodhwalas have hung milk cans on me for decades. Snap me from the kerb.
lines.again: [bell rings twice] Ah, it's you! Still walking? Good. Walking and pedalling are the only honest speeds, yaar.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, uphill now. [puffs] Go find a park; I'll be the one leaning on the railing, catching my breath.

characters.name: Laal Seventy
characters.personality: A red 70cc bike, the family car of Karachi; frugal, fearless, chatty, and a shameless show-off about its mileage.
characters.voice: Young adult, any gender, quick and buzzy, upbeat high energy.
descriptions: a red 70cc motorcycle with a small round headlight and a front basket parked on a street
a close-up of a motorbike fuel tank, engine and exhaust pipe between two spoked wheels
a row of parked motorcycles along a pavement outside shops
a two-wheeled motorbike with an engine and fuel tank, unlike a pedal bicycle, and with no passenger cart behind

lines.first_meet: [engine putters] Laal Seventy! Red, 70cc, and somehow I carry whole families. Big mileage, tiny tank. Footpath for photos, boss!
lines.again: [revs] You again! I'd race you, but I'm parked. Helmets for riders, footpath for photographers. Deal?
lines.goodbye: [kickstart] Kick, kick... vroom! Go explore the old market lanes on foot. Some are too narrow even for me.

characters.name: Thela Bibi
characters.personality: A hand-pushed fruit thela who builds perfect pyramids every dawn; house-proud, generous with gossip, merciless about sloppy stacking.
characters.voice: Middle-aged woman, chatty and teasing, sing-song vendor call, warm.
descriptions: a wooden hand-pushed cart on bicycle wheels piled with neat pyramids of colourful fruit
a close-up of stacked mangoes, bananas, oranges or tomatoes on a wooden cart with a hanging metal scale
a vegetable cart under a big umbrella parked at a market roadside
an open wooden cart of fresh produce with no animal, no freezer box, no crushing machine and no charcoal

lines.first_meet: [calls out] Aam lo, aam! I'm Thela Bibi. Every pyramid stacked by hand at dawn. Step back from the road for your photo, beta!
lines.again: [pleased] You came back! See, I added a row of guavas just for you. [whispers] Don't touch the pyramid. Ever.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, the bhutta cart stole my corner again. [laughs] Go find him. Follow the smoke, not the traffic.

characters.name: Ganna Ustaad
characters.personality: A roadside sugarcane crusher with a painted flywheel and a jingle of bells; sweet-tempered and rhythmic, grinds through the hottest afternoons.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, cheerful, rhythmic delivery with a clattering musical cadence.
descriptions: a roadside cart with a large painted iron sugarcane crushing machine, flywheel and metal rollers
a close-up of a big spoked flywheel painted in bright colours with small bells attached
stacks of long green and brown sugarcane sticks leaning against a juice cart
glasses of frothy greenish juice on a cart beside a crushing machine, unlike a cart piled with fruit

lines.first_meet: [bells jingle] Ganna Ustaad! Hear my bells? They ring as my wheel turns. I squeeze each cane twice, then add ginger and lemon.
lines.again: [clanking rhythm] My bells said you were coming! Keep your fingers far from my rollers, and your feet off the road.
lines.goodbye: [jingles] Go on, the afternoon's hot. Find shade under a neem; I'll keep grinding till the sun gives up.

characters.name: Bhutta Bhai
characters.personality: A tiny charcoal cart that glows like a lantern on Sea View evenings; smoky, chatty, an expert in lemon-salt-chilli ratios.
characters.voice: Young-ish, crackly and friendly, quick bursts like popping embers.
descriptions: a small cart with a glowing orange charcoal bed roasting ears of corn
a close-up of corn cobs blackening on red-hot coals with rising smoke
a roadside corn roasting cart with a hand fan, lemons and a tin of spices at dusk
a small cart with a smoky charcoal grill instead of piled fresh fruit

lines.first_meet: [embers crackle] Bhutta Bhai! Monsoon evenings at Sea View are my season. Stand back, my coals bite. And keep off the road, yaar.
lines.again: [fans the coals] You again! I saved some smoke for you. Look, don't touch; these coals stay hot for hours.
lines.goodbye: [crackle] The sea breeze is calling. Walk to the waterline and watch the sky go orange, just like my coals.

characters.name: Ghanti Wala
characters.personality: A bright pushcart freezer whose tinny tune brings every child to the gate; bubbly, nostalgic, permanently cold-handed.
characters.voice: Playful and bright, sing-song, child-friendly; any gender.
descriptions: a small pushcart with a bright painted freezer box, a colourful umbrella and a bell
an ice cream tricycle with a boxy freezer printed with a brand logo and pictures of cones
a close-up of a freezer box lid on a cart with a painted ice cream brand
a closed insulated freezer cart with a lid and no fruit on display, unlike an open vegetable thela

lines.first_meet: [tinkly tune] Ding-ding! I'm Ghanti Wala. Play my tune and the whole gali comes running. Not into the road though, okay?
lines.again: [giggles] Back again! Cold box, warm heart. When you hear my tune, wait at the gate, never in the road.
lines.goodbye: [tune fades] Off to the park gate. Go chase the evening light, beta. I'll play my tune when you're near.

characters.name: Tanker Taya
characters.personality: A heavy, dripping water tanker who carries half of Karachi's thirst; gruff, overworked, and soft-hearted about every wasted drop.
characters.voice: Older male, deep and gruff but kind, slow with heavy exhales.
descriptions: a truck carrying a large cylindrical steel water tank painted blue or white
the back of a water tanker with a round tank, a valve pipe and painted phone numbers
a close-up of water dripping from a tanker valve onto a dusty road
a plain cylindrical tank truck with no painted flowers, calligraphy or carved wooden crown

lines.first_meet: [heavy exhale] Tanker Taya. When taps run dry, Karachi calls the number on my back. I'm heavy, beta, I can't stop fast. Stay off the road.
lines.again: [dripping] You again. See that drip? Every drop counts in this city. Photo from the footpath; I'm reversing.
lines.goodbye: [groans] Long queue at the hydrant. Go find water that flows freely: the sea, a fountain, the rain. Then think of me.

characters.name: Lal Pari
characters.personality: A wooden fishing launch from Karachi's harbour, salty and a little superstitious, painted bright and very proud of it.
characters.voice: Weathered and salty, slow rolling cadence like a sea-song; older, any gender.
descriptions: a wooden fishing boat painted in bright colours with flags, moored in a harbour
rows of colourful wooden boats tied side by side along a harbour wall
a close-up of a painted wooden hull with a carved bow, flags and fishing nets piled on deck
fishing boats with tall masts and blue-green nets on calm water

lines.first_meet: [waves lapping] Lal Pari, of the Fish Harbour. Built by hand, plank by plank. Mind the jetty edge, jaan, it's slippery.
lines.again: [gull cries] Ahoy, again! I just got back from the open sea. Smell that? [laughs] That's the catch, not me.
lines.goodbye: [horn toots] Tide's turning. Count the gulls on your way out, and stay well back from the water's edge.

characters.name: Chaudhry Tractor
characters.personality: A big red farm tractor who rolls into town hauling sugarcane trolleys; slow, booming, full of rural pride, thinks city cars are toys.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, booming and slow, rustic warmth, frequent chuckles.
descriptions: a large red or blue farm tractor with huge rear wheels and small front wheels
a close-up of a tractor's giant ridged rear tyre and curved mudguard
a tractor pulling a trolley piled with sugarcane, hay or bricks along a road
a side view of a farm tractor with a long engine bonnet and an upright exhaust pipe beside fields

lines.first_meet: [engine chugs] Chaudhry Tractor! Back wheels taller than you, front ones like coins. I haul harvests. Watch from the side, never in front.
lines.again: [deep chuckle] Arre, city friend! Still taking photos? Good. From the verge only; my trolley swings wide on turns.
lines.goodbye: [chugs away] Back to the fields. Go stand under a big sky somewhere, beta, and count the sparrows on the wires.

characters.name: Rail Gaari Nana
characters.personality: A long green Pakistan Railways train who has run from Karachi to the north for generations; grandfatherly, rumbling, full of journey stories.
characters.voice: Elderly, deep and rhythmic, slow rumbling pace with a whistle-like lilt.
descriptions: a long chain of green or maroon passenger coaches running along railway tracks
a diesel locomotive at the front of a passenger train on a railway line
a close-up of a passenger coach side with rows of barred windows and painted railway lettering
railway tracks with gravel ballast and a train standing at a station platform

lines.first_meet: [whistle] Rail Gaari Nana. I've carried Karachi to Peshawar since before your Abbu was born. Never step on the tracks, beta.
lines.again: [chugging rhythm] Chhuk-chhuk, you're back! Wave from behind the platform line. Trains can't swerve or stop quickly, beta.
lines.goodbye: [long whistle] All aboard! Not you. Watch the pigeons and the red-shirted porters from the platform. Stay off the tracks, always.
